title: Headache
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a 55-year-old woman who presents with fever, headache, and progressive ataxia. She has developed pink macular lesions on the left thigh. Neurological examination reveals cerebellar signs. The combination of fever, neurological symptoms, and characteristic rash in the appropriate season raises concern for arboviral encephalitis. West Nile virus is the leading consideration among mosquito-borne neuroinvasive diseases. Diagnostic workup must include brain imaging to rule out stroke or mass lesion, followed by lumbar puncture for CSF analysis.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: The general examination is extremely useful to determine how sick the patient looks.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Chest / Lungs
stacks.finding: Important to look for lung pathology in a febrile patient.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Abdomen
stacks.finding: Important to look for abdominal pathology in a febrile patient.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Neuro / Psych
stacks.finding: This is the patient's chief complaint — neurologic exam is essential.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Skin
stacks.finding: This will reveal pink macular lesions on the left thigh — characteristic rash.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: Important to order a CBC with differential in a patient with fever.

stacks.label: Chest X-ray
stacks.finding: Important to get a chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia and other causes of fever.

stacks.label: Urinalysis
stacks.finding: Important to get urinalysis to rule out bacterial infection and other causes of fever.

stacks.label: Toxicology screen, urine
stacks.finding: Urine tox screen is important as illicit drugs can cause fever.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, blood
stacks.finding: Blood culture will aid in localizing the source of infection.

stacks.label: MRI/CT head
stacks.finding: Ataxia should lead to consideration of neurological infection or stroke. Brain imaging to rule out stroke or tumor. MRI preferred (more sensitive for West Nile abnormalities) but CT acceptable.

stacks.label: Lumbar puncture
stacks.finding: Lumbar puncture is essential for evaluation of patient with ataxia and fever.

stacks.label: Protein, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: CSF analysis is important in patient with fever and neurological signs.

stacks.label: Fungal culture, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: Important to culture CSF for viral, bacterial, and fungal etiologies.

stacks.label: Viral culture, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: Important to culture CSF. Note: West Nile virus is frequently negative in viral culture.

stacks.label: Bacterial culture, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: Important to culture CSF for bacterial etiologies.

stacks.label: Glucose, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: CSF glucose points toward fungal, viral, or bacterial picture. Normal glucose suggests viral (not bacterial) etiology.

stacks.label: Cell count, cerebrospinal fluid
stacks.finding: CSF cell count consistent with aseptic meningitis. Lymphocytic predominance suggests viral etiology.

stacks.label: West Nile virus antibody, CSF/serum
stacks.finding: Confirms aseptic meningitis is from West Nile virus.

stacks.label: HSV PCR, CSF/serum
stacks.finding: Aseptic meningitis workup should include herpes simplex screening.

stacks.label: Basic metabolic profile / Comprehensive metabolic profile / Liver function panel
stacks.finding: Chemistries are an important screening tool and should be done in nearly every non-emergent patient.

stacks.label: Tdap vaccine
stacks.finding: Tdap should be given every 10 years. No history given — should be administered.

stacks.label: Papanicolaou smear
stacks.finding: HPV DNA test every 3 years for women ≥30 with normal cytology. No history given — should be scheduled.

stacks.label: Mammography
stacks.finding: USPSTF recommends mammogram screening every 2 years for patients ages 50-69.

physical_exam.neurological: Ataxia — cerebellar findings. Fever with neurological signs = CNS infection until proven otherwise. Assess for nuchal rigidity, photophobia, focal deficits.
physical_exam.skin: Pink macular lesions on left thigh — characteristic of West Nile virus exanthem.

decoys.label: Empiric antibiotics without LP
decoys.reason_wrong: Bacterial meningitis is on the differential and requires CSF culture before antibiotics. But this is viral encephalitis — LP is diagnostic, not empiric.

decoys.label: Corticosteroids
decoys.reason_wrong: No evidence for steroids in West Nile encephalitis. Supportive care is the mainstay.

decoys.label: Discharge from office
decoys.reason_wrong: Patient with encephalitis requires inpatient monitoring. West Nile can progress to flaccid paralysis and respiratory failure.

teach_me_steps.reasoning: Rule out mass lesion, stroke, or herniation risk before lumbar puncture. MRI more sensitive for West Nile abnormalities.

teach_me_steps.order: Lumbar puncture with full CSF analysis
teach_me_steps.reasoning: CSF: cell count, protein, glucose, bacterial/viral/fungal cultures. Lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal glucose = viral picture.
Confirmatory test. Note: WNV viral culture is frequently negative — antibody testing is key.
Encephalitis requires monitored bed. Can progress to flaccid paralysis and respiratory failure.
No specific antiviral for WNV. Treatment is supportive — IV fluids, monitoring, respiratory support if needed.

case_summary: Difficult diagnostic case — West Nile encephalitis. Fever + ataxia + maculopapular rash. CT/MRI to rule out stroke/mass → LP with CSF analysis (lymphocytic pleocytosis, normal glucose, elevated protein = viral) → WNV antibody confirms. Little treatment — supportive care. Preventive health: Pap, mammogram, Tdap.
